nwm-stas-lookup.source: NWM / NextGen recipe: soil texture class -> STAS SOILPARM.TBL row; Noah/Noah-MP SOILPARM.TBL section STAS (the NWM soil class table), as shipped in NOAA-OWP/ngen be11a180565a78ff069d855b0b5dbfc23845e7d8 data/gauge_01073000/NOAH/parameters/SOILPARM.TBL (Apache-2.0); class values after Cosby et al. (1984), Water Resour. Res. 20(6):682-690

aggregation.soil_class: area mode over all classes, water and ice included (Noah-OWP isltyp)
aggregation.soil_b: b of the area-modal hydraulic class (NextGen hydrofabric divide attribute mode.bexp)
aggregation.soil_satdk_m_s: area-weighted geometric mean over hydraulic classes (geom_mean.dksat)
aggregation.soil_satpsi_m: area-weighted geometric mean over hydraulic classes (geom_mean.psisat)
aggregation.soil_smcmax: area-weighted arithmetic mean over hydraulic classes (mean.smcmax)
aggregation.soil_wltsmc: area-weighted arithmetic mean over hydraulic classes (mean.smcwlt)

cosby1984-continuous.source: Cosby, Hornberger, Clapp and Ginn (1984), Water Resour. Res. 20(6):682-690, Table 4 multivariate regressions on sand/silt/clay %; wilting point from the Campbell (1974, Soil Sci. 117:311-314) retention curve at 150 m (1.5 MPa)

aggregation.soil_b: area-weighted arithmetic mean of the per-cell regression value

lgar-c-default-vg.source: NOAA-OWP/LGAR-C 9166bcfa1d8c37af26a4f6329872400f07a33ff6 data/vG_default_params.dat (Apache-2.0): the LGAR default van Genuchten parameters per USDA texture class

soil_depth_m.source: CFE soil_params.depth in every NextGen example packet (NOAA-OWP/ngen be11a180565a78ff069d855b0b5dbfc23845e7d8 data/gauge_01073000/CFE/cat-*_bmi_config_cfe_pass.txt (Apache-2.0), the NextGen example CFE packets the CONUS lanes replay); the 2 m Noah-MP four-layer column the NWM runs

refkdt.source: Schaake et al. (1996), J. Geophys. Res. 101(D3):7461-7475 surface-runoff parameter; the uncalibrated Noah/NWM default REFKDT_DATA = 3.0 (GENPARM.TBL in ngen be11a180 data/gauge_01073000/NOAH/parameters); NWM values are calibrated per basin

alpha_fc.source: CFE field-capacity fraction alpha_fc in every NextGen example packet (NOAA-OWP/ngen be11a180565a78ff069d855b0b5dbfc23845e7d8 data/gauge_01073000/CFE/cat-*_bmi_config_cfe_pass.txt (Apache-2.0), the NextGen example CFE packets the CONUS lanes replay)

k_lf.source: CFE lateral-flow coefficient K_lf in every NextGen example packet (NOAA-OWP/ngen be11a180565a78ff069d855b0b5dbfc23845e7d8 data/gauge_01073000/CFE/cat-*_bmi_config_cfe_pass.txt (Apache-2.0), the NextGen example CFE packets the CONUS lanes replay)

k_nash.source: CFE Nash-cascade coefficient K_nash in every NextGen example packet (NOAA-OWP/ngen be11a180565a78ff069d855b0b5dbfc23845e7d8 data/gauge_01073000/CFE/cat-*_bmi_config_cfe_pass.txt (Apache-2.0), the NextGen example CFE packets the CONUS lanes replay); two Nash reservoirs (nash_storage=0.0,0.0)

max_gw_storage_m.source: NOAA NWM v3.1.6 GWBUCKPARM_CONUS_FullRouting.nc (https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/codes/nwprod/nwm.v3.1.6/parm/domain/GWBUCKPARM_CONUS_FullRouting.nc, sha256 27b815ad99ffb3adf3cc38c7c677a33ba29630c60d8336788ba2b9cb9053f3e3), 2724837 CONUS buckets: CONUS median of the calibrated Zmax 91.7537 mm (p05 11.46, p95 247.32 mm), converted to m as the NextGen packets carry it

gw_coeff_m3_s.source: NOAA NWM v3.1.6 GWBUCKPARM_CONUS_FullRouting.nc (https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/codes/nwprod/nwm.v3.1.6/parm/domain/GWBUCKPARM_CONUS_FullRouting.nc, sha256 27b815ad99ffb3adf3cc38c7c677a33ba29630c60d8336788ba2b9cb9053f3e3), 2724837 CONUS buckets: Coeff is 0.005..0.005 (one value) for every bucket. CFE Cgw [m h-1] = Coeff * 3600 / catchment area [m2] (the NWM bucket outflow Q = Coeff (exp(Expon z/Zmax) - 1) is a volume rate per catchment; CFE takes the same law as a depth rate)

gw_expon.source: NOAA NWM v3.1.6 GWBUCKPARM_CONUS_FullRouting.nc (https://www.nco.ncep.noaa.gov/pmb/codes/nwprod/nwm.v3.1.6/parm/domain/GWBUCKPARM_CONUS_FullRouting.nc, sha256 27b815ad99ffb3adf3cc38c7c677a33ba29630c60d8336788ba2b9cb9053f3e3), 2724837 CONUS buckets: CONUS median of the calibrated Expon (p05 1.044, p95 7.825); a national prior where no calibration exists

soil_color.source: Noah-OWP soilcolor in every NextGen example namelist (ngen be11a180 data/gauge_01073000/NOAH/cat-*.input soilcolor = 4)

slop.source: Noah/NWM uncalibrated drainage slope coefficient SLOPE_DATA category 1 = 0.1 (GENPARM.TBL in ngen be11a180 data/gauge_01073000/NOAH/parameters). CFE soil_params.slop is this drainage coefficient: the NWM v3.1.6 soilproperties 'slope' field it is taken from carries calibrated values clustered around 0.1 (0.057, 0.1, 0.24 over the Russian River), not terrain slope. Alternative method terrain_tan_coarse (mean tan(slope) of the DEM at coarse_m) stays selectable; it matched NWM worse (median ratio 0.69, 51 % within 2x)

giuh.source: time-area GIUH (Clark 1945; Maidment et al. 1996, Hydrol. Process. 10:831-844) on Priority-Flood paths (Barnes et al. 2014) to the catchment outlet; V = k S^0.5 with k from USDA-NRCS (2010) National Engineering Handbook Part 630 Hydrology, ch. 15, Table 15-3 (V = k S^0.5, V ft/s, S ft/ft); slope floored at 0.005 m/m; channel initiation 0.5 km2, inside the 0.01-0.5 km2 range of field channel heads (Montgomery and Dietrich 1988, Nature 336:232-234); ordinates per CFE step of 3600 s

example-packet-priors.source: K_lf 0.01, K_nash 0.03, alpha_fc 0.33 from constants: the NextGen example CFE packets (NOAA-OWP/ngen be11a180565a78ff069d855b0b5dbfc23845e7d8 data/gauge_01073000/CFE/cat-*_bmi_config_cfe_pass.txt (Apache-2.0), the NextGen example CFE packets the CONUS lanes replay); the priors the 2026-10-18 Rhine proof ran with (peaks about 4 days late)

hillslope-kinematic-v1.source: Regionalised CFE subsurface parameters from catchment attributes. K_lf (m/h) = 3600 * 2 F Ks sin(b) D / L: Sloan and Moore (1984), Modeling subsurface stormflow on steeply sloping forested watersheds, Water Resour. Res. 20(12):1815-1822, kinematic storage model (linear drainage constant 2 Ks sin(b) / (theta_d L)) applied to the CFE lateral outlet K_lf (S - S_fc)/(S_max - S_fc), S_max - S_fc = D theta_d. K_nash (1/h) = N 3600 F Ks sin(b) / (theta_d L): Beven (1981), Kinematic subsurface stormflow, Water Resour. Res. 17(5):1419-1424 (celerity F Ks sin(b)/theta_d), hillslope travel time L/c shared over a Nash (1957, IASH Publ. 45(3):114-121) cascade of N reservoirs. L = mean Priority-Flood flow distance from hillslope cells to the first channel cell on Copernicus GLO-90 (Horton 1945 overland-flow length, Geol. Soc. Am. Bull. 56(3):275-370, measured on the paths), sin(b) = mean hillslope Horn slope; Ks = catchment satdk (SoilGrids texture -> STAS); theta_d = smcmax - theta_fc with theta_fc on the Clapp and Hornberger (1978, Water Resour. Res. 14(4):601-604) curve at the field-capacity head alpha_fc * 10.33 m. This is the starting point for an uncalibrated basin anywhere; gauged basins are calibrated by the gauge-calibration door (tools/hydro_world_calibration) and ungauged ones take the Gower (1971) nearest calibrated donor.
hillslope-kinematic-v1.lateral_ksat_factor_source: F, the lateral to vertical saturated conductivity ratio of the hillslope (macropores, layering): LKSATFAC = 1000, the default lateral saturated conductivity multiplier of the NCAR WRF-Hydro subsurface routing (Gochis et al. 2020, The WRF-Hydro Modeling System Technical Description, Version 5.1.1, NCAR Technical Note, cited as a publication; no UCAR code used)
hillslope-kinematic-v1.alpha_fc_source: Field capacity as the water held at 1/3 bar (Richards and Weaver 1944, Soil Sci. 58:207-218; the CFE alpha_fc = 0.33 convention), and at 1/10 bar for coarse-textured soils (STAS 1 SAND, 2 LOAMY SAND), as USDA-NRCS National Soil Survey Handbook Part 618 takes the upper end of available water capacity
